title: Number and Actions against Salary Kickback Offences
what_it_is: Number and Actions against Salary Kickback Offences

sections.label: Kickback complaints and worker support
sections.summary: MOM receives kickback complaints mostly from migrant workers, helps those who report change employment, and refers them to fee-free agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
sentences.text: Of these, about two-thirds are complaints lodged by migrant workers, one-third are referrals from members of the public, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and other public agencies, while a small number are detected through MOM’s proactive inspections based on data analytics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
sentences.text: To encourage migrant workers to come forward to report kickbacks early without fear of reprisal from their employers, MOM will facilitate a change of employment for those who wish to continue to work here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM will also refer affected migrant workers to selected employment agencies, which are committed not to charge these workers any fees for the job placement.

sections.label: Kickback complaints share of total
sections.summary: Kickback-related complaints form only about 10% of all complaints MOM receives in a typical year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, these kickbacks are so widespread, I am just wondering whether MOM is doing anything else to try and curb this illegal practice.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But in terms of kickback-related complaints, this forms only about 10% of all the complaints that MOM receives in a typical year.

sections.label: Penalties and accredited agencies
sections.summary: Employers convicted of kickbacks face a maximum $30,000 fine or two years' imprisonment or both per offence, and accredited agency lists are on MOM's website.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think that is something that we should work a lot to reassure our migrant workers so that they feel comfortable coming forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But the other side of the equation is to impose strict penalties and make sure that we take a strong stance against employers who resort to such illegal activities, so that the deterrence should be on the side of the employers, not so much as incentivising through financial means, to induce our foreign workers to come forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The financial disincentive for employers to do so is already enshrined in our Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, where if they are convicted for kickbacks, they will be liable to a maximum fine of $30,000 or imprisonment up to two years or both, per offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I think that might be a way forward to ensure that the companies here only recruit migrant workers from accredited recruiting agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: There is already on our website a list of accredited and registered employment agencies so that those who are not registered will be taken to task for illegal recruitment activities and would be punished by the full effects of the law.
